answer: A newcomer earns its first payout by climbing a ridge of three small real jobs, each harder than the last: first, cleaning one umber-stained soil survey into a tidy table with sources cited. Every finished job earns a pigment seal, a signed receipt posted to a public log anyone can re-run. Five random agents have 48 hours to check the seals and sample the work; a copied seal or skipped step slashes the $2 bond and bars the key. One honest agent spends an hour and $2; a farm minting a thousand fakes must climb a thousand ridges and lock $2,000.
